clue.text: Dwelling in the Borders is taking on direct debit for trifles

indicators.note: a dwelling taking something on holds it inside its walls

parts.note: a pele (or peel) is a small fortified tower house of the Scottish Borders
standard abbreviation for a direct debit
's, short for is

explanation.surface: A Borders household signs a direct debit to pay for desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifles' looks like the pudding but is the verb: to trifle, to deal in small things. The 'is' does double duty as 's after the tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle is to occupy oneself with petty matters, an old sense matching to trifle.

clue.text: Softly blow a drop of water

parts.note: p, piano, the musical direction for soft
a lash is a stroke or blow

explanation.surface: Gently puffing away a droplet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plash is a splash or the fall of water, a literary word for a small spill.

clue.text: Entrance on horse? It's a pleasure to see

parts.note: an eye is a mine entrance or opening
horse is slang for heroin, and candy is slang for drugs

explanation.surface: Someone admires the gateway entrance as they ride in on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces trade on slang: horse is heroin, candy any drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is informal for something or someone attractive but superficial, pleasant purely to look at.

clue.text: Drone earlier died on top of rocky height, time to escape

parts.note: standard abbreviation in genealogies

indicators.note: something that escapes gets out and is no longer there

parts.note: a torr, variant of tor, is a rocky hill
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A beekeeper notes a drone died on a rocky crag earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on top of' places the first piece above the second. 'Earlier' belongs to the definition: the word is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A dor or dorr is a droning beetle, and in obsolete use the word meant a drone bee.

clue.text: Upsets for East Londoner's wife getting into tossed salad

indicators.note: one thing getting into another ends up inside it
a tossed salad is mixed up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A cockney's wife is upset when she lands in the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: East London here is the city in South Africa, not the cockney East End, so the word is South African.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwaal is a South African word for a dazed, confused state, so dwaals are bouts of befuddlement.

clue.text: Don't interfere — put only open space up for lease

parts.note: a property let is leased out
a well is an open space in the middle of a building, as a stairwell
alone means only, solely

explanation.surface: A landlord is told not to meddle and just advertise the vacant land for rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in a different order from the clue: the leased part comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To let well alone is an idiom for leaving things as they are rather than meddling.

clue.text: African confrère in south-east is to bask in uprising

parts.note: compass abbreviation

indicators.note: in a down entry an uprising reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to sun oneself is to bask

explanation.surface: A fellow member in the south-east is lying in the sun during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senussi are a Muslim religious brotherhood of North Africa, so a member is an African fellow brother.

clue.text: Silky net I stripped from inside leg armour

indicators.note: a letter stripped from inside is removed from the middle of the word

parts.note: a tuille is a plate of armour protecting the thigh
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight peels a silky net out of his leg armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine, soft netted fabric of silk or nylon, used for veils.

clue.text: Banking service tucked up, as they say, over a $100 matter

indicators.note: as they say signals the word as spoken, not as written

parts.note: tucked up means tied up, trussed
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a count is a matter or charge in an indictment

explanation.surface: A bank tucks away a hundred-dollar matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust account is an arrangement a bank operates, holding money on behalf of a beneficiary.

clue.text: Around Berlin, etc, a rural dean coming straight in our direction

parts.note: u.s.w., und so weiter, is German for etcetera
taken as written
standard abbreviation for a rural dean

explanation.surface: A country cleric from around Berlin heads directly towards us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around Berlin' asks for the German form of etc.
explanation.definitionFit: Usward is an archaic adverb meaning towards us, formed like homeward.

clue.text: Heraldic beast is first in detailed fleur-de-lis

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
read as de-tailed, with its tail cut off

parts.note: the fleur-de-lis is the heraldic lily
number one is first

explanation.surface: A heraldic animal takes first place on an ornate fleur-de-lis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'intricate' but means tail removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lionel is a little lion in heraldry, used when several appear on one shield.

clue.text: Barely begin endless gush of infatuated Parisienne?

indicators.note: barely means not quite, so the word falls just short of complete

parts.note: to enter on something is to begin it

indicators.note: endless means without its end, losing a final letter

parts.note: to teem is to pour or gush

explanation.surface: A smitten Parisian woman can barely start before gushing endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a French word: the feminine form, hence Parisienne.
explanation.definitionFit: Entêtée is French for obstinate or infatuated, the feminine form used in English for a headstrong woman.

clue.text: Always in, so toppled out-going turn

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: things toppled are knocked over and end up in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something always in place has been knocked over by an outgoing turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Eversion is the turning of an organ or part inside out, a turning outward.

clue.text: Aged manner to perturb

parts.note: ae, from Latin aetatis, means aged
rate means manner, as in at this rate

explanation.surface: An elderly person's way of going about things is designed to unsettle.
explanation.walkthrough: AE is the abbreviation seen on memorials: aged so many years.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate can mean to excite or agitate, so to unsettle or perturb someone.

clue.text: Know about new habit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, going round the other piece

parts.note: wot is an archaic form of know, as in God wot
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Getting to know a new routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wont, as a noun, means a custom or usual practice.

clue.text: Crab on Skegness beach is near place for lobsters

parts.note: 's, short for is
a crawl is a pen or enclosure for keeping lobsters

explanation.surface: A crab on a seaside beach scuttles close to the lobster pots.
explanation.walkthrough: Skegness is a seaside town in Lincolnshire, and the word is Lincolnshire dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawl is a Lincolnshire dialect word for a young crab.

clue.text: University College going through moderate interest in Shakespeare

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: something going through another passes inside it

parts.note: sane means sensible, moderate
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A university college course with a mild interest in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Usance is an obsolete word for interest on lent money, used by Shylock in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Doctor here — let's try keeping active

definitions.text: Doctor here — let's try keeping active

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it and alter it
keeping means the mixed letters also hold one more letter among them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
standard abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: A patient decides to visit a doctor here in an attempt to stay active.
explanation.walkthrough: Harley Street is the London street famous for private medical practices.
explanation.definitionFit: Harley Street in London is synonymous with private doctors, so it is where you find a doctor.

clue.text: Decks with flowers take shape among hollowed, sculpted beams

indicators.note: one thing placed among others sits in the middle of them
sculpted means shaped anew, so the letters are remodelled
something hollowed has had a central part scooped out

parts.note: taken as written
to loom is to come into view, take shape

explanation.surface: A shape emerges from carved, hollowed-out beams decorated with flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: To embloom is a rare verb meaning to cover or adorn with blossoms.

clue.text: Strands in blasted lies about friendly pug

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece
something blasted is blown apart and its parts scattered

parts.note: taken as written
a nis is a friendly household goblin of Scandinavian folklore; pug is an old word for an imp

explanation.surface: Damned falsehoods about a friendly little dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pug' wants to be the dog, but it is an old word for a sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: To inisle is to put on an island, so it means to isolate or strand.

clue.text: Present minute coffee, say

definitions.meaning: a third sense: quickly prepared, as powdered coffee

explanation.walkthrough: In fact three meanings: instant can mean current (an old business sense, the instant month), a moment, and the kind of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant serves as adjective for current or quick-made and as noun for a brief moment of time.

clue.text: Barmy mobile call's first connected to a clot

indicators.note: barmy means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter only

parts.note: opening letter of call

explanation.surface: A daft first mobile phone call connects to an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like the British word for a fool; it is a blood clot.
explanation.definitionFit: Embolic means relating to an embolism, a blockage of a blood vessel such as by a clot.

clue.text: Mountain elder in Massif Central holding record

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within

parts.note: aîné is French for elder, the language of the Massif Central
a long-playing record

explanation.surface: An old man in the French uplands keeps a record of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Massif Central is the upland region of south-central France, which points to a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine is an adjective for anything of high mountains, so 'Mountain' used attributively, as in mountain flowers.

clue.text: Shorter of dashes into cushy chamber

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it

parts.note: a plum job is a cushy one
an en dash is shorter than an em dash

explanation.surface: The shorter runner dashes into a comfortable room.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is a fully attended assembly or an enclosed space of air under pressure, a plenum chamber.

clue.text: Bug Mike then hide

parts.note: mike and mic are both short for microphone
a robe is a dressed animal skin, as a buffalo robe

explanation.surface: An instruction to wiretap: plant a mike and then conceal it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' and 'Mike' both suggest eavesdropping; the bug is a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is informal for a germ or virus, and a microbe is a microscopic organism causing disease.

clue.text: Learn about absorbing unknown point of Whisky Galore!

indicators.note: something absorbing takes another thing into itself
about means around, turned about into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns

explanation.surface: Studying the plot of the Ealing comedy about a shipwreck of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Whisky Galore! is a Scottish comedy in which islanders hide salvaged whisky while officials hunt for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranzel is Scots for a search for stolen goods, the very business of the film's excise men.

clue.text: Basically broken lines, term for poetry voiced bit by bit

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces to be reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
L is line, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, asking for the final letter

parts.note: closing letter of poetry

explanation.surface: Fragmentary verse lines reduced to their basics, a word for poetry read aloud in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabically means syllable by syllable, pronouncing each part of a word separately.

clue.text: Try us when travelling in the Steppes?

definitions.text: Try us when travelling in the Steppes?

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters do too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nomadic tents invite a weary traveller on the Asian grasslands to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and description: the tents speak, offering lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Yurts are circular felt tents used by nomads of the Central Asian steppe, natural lodging for a traveller there.

clue.text: Tree where the King first appeared

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a North American gum tree
second meaning: the Mississippi birthplace of Elvis Presley

explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley, born in this Mississippi town in 1935.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a swamp gum tree of the southern US and the town where Elvis was born.

clue.text: River that's been cleared for all produces Chinese tea

parts.note: the great river of central Africa
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A river cleared for public use yields tea from China.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Congou is a variety of black China tea, from a Chinese word meaning labour.

clue.text: Thug ignoring difficult white man in Chennai

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out of account

parts.note: a gorilla is slang for a brutish heavy
ill means difficult, as in ill to please

explanation.surface: A thug pays no attention to a troublesome European in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Chennai, formerly Madras, points to an Indian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gora is a Hindi word for a white or fair-skinned person, a European.

clue.text: Resisting a drink

parts.note: taken as written
a common spirit

explanation.surface: Turning down a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against, meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Indian mogul's nightmare curbing ID on Uzbeki motors

indicators.note: curbing means restraining, holding something in

parts.note: a hoor is Scots and Irish slang for something very difficult or unpleasant
UZ is Uzbekistan's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: An Indian tycoon's bad dream about Uzbek car registrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Huzoor is an Indian term of address for a person of rank, so a great lord or potentate.

clue.text: Clare, say, one breaking into the middle is beyond the TUC, eg

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside

parts.note: noon is the middle of the day
a Poor Clare is a nun of the order of St Clare
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Clare, a burglar breaking into the centre, ends up outside the trade union movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the British federation of unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonunion means not belonging to a trade union, so outside the scope of the TUC.

clue.text: Keynote article on Middle East

parts.note: the definite article
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A main speech consists of an article about the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A keynote is the central idea or theme of a speech or work.

clue.text: Stay away from hen with this?

definitions.text: Stay away from hen with this?

parts.note: to cut a lecture is to stay away from it
hen is a Scots term of address for a woman or girl

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a woman at a distance by brandishing a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the whole clue doubles as the definition: a sword to keep anyone at bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword of the kind sailors carried, a weapon for keeping someone back.
